skill.name: commit-chat-push
skill.description: Guides Codex through reviewing changes, exporting a redacted session transcript, committing both the code and transcript, and pushing the branch.
skill.summary: Commit code changes with a redacted Codex session transcript.
skill.author: bertona88

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown examples, fixed Git checks, or defensive secret scans. The material risk is the intended export, commit, and push of Codex session transcripts from ~/.codex/sessions. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files, but the referenced redaction exporter was not present in the scanned package.

remediation.issue: Codex session transcripts may expose sensitive prompts, commands, paths, or project context.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval after showing the transcript path, target remote, staged files, and secret scan result.

remediation.issue: The redaction exporter referenced by the skill is not present in the scanned files.
remediation.suggestion: Ship the exporter with the skill and include tests that prove system messages, secrets, and raw logs are omitted.

remediation.issue: The workflow allows raw Codex JSONL logs to be committed after a warning.
remediation.suggestion: Remove raw JSONL commits from the workflow or require a separate explicit confirmation for private repositories only.

remediation.issue: Push steps can publish transcript content to a remote repository.
remediation.suggestion: Stop before git push unless the user confirms the remote, branch, transcript review, and staged diff.

semantic_findings.title: AI Session Transcript Publication Risk
semantic_findings.description: The skill is designed to export Codex session content, commit it with code changes, and push the branch. Even redacted transcripts can expose prompts, commands, local paths, and sensitive project context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The README and SKILL.md both describe exporting Codex sessions and pushing commits. The files also acknowledge that raw sessions and command output can contain sensitive material.

semantic_findings.title: Referenced Redaction Exporter Is Not Reviewable
semantic_findings.description: The workflow depends on export_codex_session.py for transcript creation and redaction, but the scanned package contains no script file. This makes the advertised redaction behavior unverifiable from the reviewed files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reviewed file set contains README.md, SKILL.md, and .gitignore only, while both docs reference an exporter script. The risk is confidence-limited because the script may exist outside the scanned package.

content.value_statement: Teams need a clear record of which AI session produced a code change. This skill guides Codex through transcript export, review, commit, and push steps.
actual_capabilities: Guides Codex through Git status, diff review, staging, commit, and push checks.
Documents a workflow for exporting a Markdown transcript from Codex session logs.
Uses an anchor marker approach to select the intended Codex session.
Recommends scanning exported transcripts for common secret patterns before committing.
Advises against staging unrelated dirty files or force-pushing without explicit user approval.
Documents transcript output locations and exporter options for provenance records.
limitations: It cannot guarantee every secret or private detail is removed from a transcript.
The referenced exporter script is not present in the scanned skill files.
It assumes the repository uses Git and has an appropriate remote configured.
It does not replace human review before publishing a transcript to source control.

use_cases.title: Record AI-assisted feature work
use_cases.description: Commit finished code with a reviewed transcript that explains the AI-assisted implementation session.

use_cases.title: Preserve review evidence
use_cases.description: Create a source-controlled provenance trail for changes that need later audit or handoff.

use_cases.title: Standardize commit hygiene
use_cases.description: Use repeatable checks for repository status, transcript review, staging, commit, and push behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Commit Current Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a standard provenance commit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my changes, export the Codex session transcript, commit both, and push the branch.

prompt_templates.title: Commit Selected Files
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the worktree has unrelated local changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill, but stage only the files for this task. Leave unrelated dirty files untouched and include the transcript.

prompt_templates.title: Review Before Push
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a human wants to inspect the transcript first.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to prepare the commit and transcript. Stop before pushing so I can review the staged changes.

prompt_templates.title: Strict Provenance Commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with explicit privacy controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill with anchor-based session selection. Scan the transcript for secrets, summarize risks, commit approved files, then push only after confirmation.

output_examples.input: Commit the finished feature and include the Codex chat transcript.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports reviewed changes, transcript path, tests run, commit hash, push result, and any privacy warnings.

output_examples.input: Prepare the provenance commit, but do not push yet.
output_examples.output: The assistant exports and reviews the transcript, stages intended files, shows the planned commit summary, and waits for approval.

output_examples.input: Commit only my bug fix files and leave my local notes alone.
output_examples.output: The assistant separates unrelated files, stages only approved paths, includes the transcript, and explains what was left unstaged.

best_practices: Review the exported transcript before staging it for commit.
Use anchor-based session selection to avoid exporting the wrong session.
Confirm the Git remote and staged file list before pushing.
anti_patterns: Do not commit raw Codex JSONL session files to a repository.
Do not rely on redaction without a manual secret review.
Do not use broad staging when unrelated local changes are present.

faq.question: What does this skill add to a normal commit?
faq.answer: It adds a workflow for including a reviewed Codex session transcript with the code change.

faq.question: Does it automatically remove all secrets?
faq.answer: No. It describes redaction and secret scanning, but users must still review the transcript.

faq.question: Can it work without a Git remote?
faq.answer: It can guide local commit preparation, but push steps require a configured Git remote.

faq.question: Why does it use an anchor marker?
faq.answer: The marker helps select the intended Codex session when several sessions share the same repository.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: It can be used privately, but transcripts may contain sensitive context and need careful review.

faq.question: Does the scanned package include the exporter script?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed files reference the exporter, but the script was not present in the scanned file set.
